issue.title: Drain stranded agents when an LLM provider is disabled
issue.description: Disabling a provider — automatically on a usage limit or by hand in Launch Control — relaunches the agents that provider stranded, and says exactly what moved and what did not.

issue.title: Provider-drain planning and execution engine
issue.description: engine: select the agents a disabled provider stranded, classify each one's reroute or refusal through the existing restart and launch-guard machinery, and execute the moves.

issue.title: sase agent drain command and durable operation
issue.description: cli: add the `sase agent drain` subcommand with preview, confirmation, receipt, and JSON envelope, and register it as the `agent.drain` durable operation.

issue.title: Automatic drain on a usage-limit disable
issue.description: auto: gate the feature behind a beta flag, submit a drain proc when a usage-limit disable wins its first-writer window, and make that drain own the single enriched usage-limit notification.

issue.title: Launch Control relaunch prompt after a manual disable
issue.description: ace: after a manual hard disable in the Models panel, offer a single-keypress relaunch chooser and submit the drain as a durable tracked proc.

issue.title: End-to-end drill and reference documentation
issue.description: soak: prove the whole loop through the fakey provider end to end and document draining in the LLM provider reference.

Whichever phase (sase-su.2) actually consumes plan_provider_drain/execute_provider_drain should drop these two now-unnecessary --epic-symbol entries from the Justfile before it or the epic closes.

Gated automatic provider drain behind new beta flag provider_drain (bead sase-sx). Added llm_provider.usage_limit.relaunch/relaunch_limit config (default_config.yml, sase.schema.json, docs/configuration.md, docs/llms.md bullets). usage_limit_disable.py now submits a durable 'sase agent drain' proc (via sase.procs.submit_proc_request, operation=agent.drain) instead of notifying inline when the flag is on, relaunch is enabled, and the disable is hard; falls back to inline notify if submission raises or preconditions aren't met. sase agent drain's ops-layer dispatcher (_run_drain) now loads the operation request payload, settles the trigger agent via a bounded 60s wait_watch poll before planning, and owns sending the one enriched usage-limit notification (new _agent_drain_notify.py module) built from the same JSON envelope the CLI reports; notify_provider_usage_limit_disabled() gained an optional drain_notes param rendered by _drain_render.usage_limit_drain_report_notes(). Verified: just install; just check (all lint gates green, including symvision after removing 2 pre-existing stale --epic-symbol entries from a closed epic plus one my own change made stale); ruff/mypy clean; the full scoped test suite passed except 8 pre-existing failures in test_launch_proc_runtime.py/test_direct_typed_launch.py that reproduce identically on a clean master checkout (unrelated environment flake, noted as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP); targeted re-run of every new/changed test file (106 tests) passed cleanly.

No --epic-symbol entries for this bead.

LANDED epic sase-su (provider drain) at HEAD ad9ed74af.

VERIFIED (step 1). Read all five phase beads, every note, the linked plan
(plan:202608/provider_drain.md), and the five epic commits (bf3206b8f engine,
f13361ca3 CLI, d06d268ea auto-drain, 54ede7fa5 ACE prompt, ad9ed74af docs+e2e),
then read the shipped source rather than trusting the phase reports. Confirmed
against the plan's acceptance list:

- Engine (sase.agent.provider_drain + _drain_types/_drain_selection/
  _drain_planning/_drain_execute) is read-only in planning and never raises for
  one bad row. Selection honours effective-provider precedence
  (exec_llm_provider else listed llm_provider), the 300s FAILED grace window
  gated on detect_usage_limit(), least-progress-first ordering, and drops
  monitor / QUESTION-ANSWERED / caller rows as reported skips.
- Route classification really does go through plan_launch_units(), which
  resolves with consume=False and so does not advance a pooled cursor.
  plan_agent_restart() rebuilds from raw_xprompt.md, so an alias-spelled prompt
  reroutes and a pinned provider/model prompt is honestly reported stranded
  instead of guessed onto a substitute.
- `sase agent drain` matches the plan's exit contract (0 drained/previewed,
  2 refused with nothing changed, 1 at least one move failed after execution
  started); --help confirms -j/-l/-m/-n/-y plus the -Q/-R operation sidecars.
- Exactly one notification per disable window in both paths: _notify_or_drain()
  notifies inline unless flag+relaunch+hard, and falls back to the inline
  notification when submit_proc_request raises; the drain proc sends its one
  enriched notification from run_agents_drain's finally-block report_fn.
- ACE prompt computes its preview off the event loop in the provider-routing-write
  worker, stays silent on an empty preview / soft disable / flag off, and
  re-plans inside the proc rather than acting on the stale preview. Its
  concurrency key provider-drain:<provider> matches the automatic path's, so the
  two dedup against each other; the site is registered in the proc-producer
  inventory.
- Flag provider_drain is a real beta flag with removal bead sase-sx (left open
  by design). No new durable state: results live in the proc result envelope.
- Ran the drain suites myself: 115 tests across
  test_agent_provider_drain_{selection,plan,execute}, test_agent_drain_cli,
  test_agent_drain_usage_limit_report, test_ops_agent_drain_notify,
  test_llm_provider_usage_limit_disable, test_models_panel_provider_modal and
  ace/tui/test_provider_drain_prompt_panel -- all pass.
- The epic bead's own DISCOVERED ISSUE (redundant sase-su.2 --epic-symbol
  entries) was addressed: f13361ca3 removed both Justfile lines, and
  `sase bead epic-symbols sase-su` reports no entries.

INTEGRATED (step 2). Reviewed all 20 non-epic commits that landed between
bf3206b8f~1 and HEAD and every file they touch that intersects the drain's
surface. Findings, all already-integrated with no code change required:

- b59b04651 (reserve pooled alias selections at launch) is the only one that
  could have broken the drain. It does not: launch_guard._resolve_candidate
  calls resolve_launch_selection(consume=False), so drain planning still never
  consumes a pool cursor, and the reservation now published in agent_meta.json
  makes a STARTING/WAITING row's provider MORE reliable for _matches_provider,
  not less.
- 1b2381366 (deterministic family-root kill-and-edit name reuse) changed
  sase.agent.names, which the drain reaches only through plan_agent_restart;
  the restart refusal set is unchanged (not_found, no_prompt, multi_segment,
  fanout, container, identity, name_not_reusable, preflight) and the drain
  passes every reason through verbatim, so the fix is inherited.
- aeae0bb8f (base_env through standalone proc launch runtime) and 2a139761e
  (suppress clean proc admission notifications) both act on the generic proc
  path the drain submits into; the drain benefits with no drain-specific
  branch. tests/test_launch_proc_runtime.py + the direct-typed-launch node all
  pass here.
- No non-epic commit touched notifications/senders.py after d06d268ea, and the
  soft-enable path in _launch_provider_guard.py still writes only soft
  disables, so it correctly never prompts.
- Nothing landed that duplicates the drain or that should now call it.
